assessment.rationale: No open or discoverable solution provides a decent home for every family, so the Main KPI of 2,000,000,000 people newly housed is unmet. UN-Habitat estimates about 100 million people are homeless, about one in four live in housing that harms their health, safety and prosperity, and about 3 billion people (40% of the world) will need adequate housing by 2030, which requires 96,000 new affordable units every day (https://unhabitat.org/topic/housing). The largest programmes are national subsidy schemes such as India's PMAY-Gramin, whose evaluations are regional and descriptive (https://doi.org/10.56975/ijcrt.v13i6.288811), and the lower-cost construction routes remain unproven at scale: a 2026 review of 3D-printed affordable housing finds unresolved scalability, cost and regulatory barriers (https://doi.org/10.3390/buildings16020343). Honest limit: building methods, subsidy and cooperative housing models are known and published, so this is chiefly a finance, land and governance problem, and tasks that restate known programmes are not new work; tasks must target a new, checkable piece, such as a verified cost-per-unit reduction method, a land-tenure or targeting method, or a validated housing-adequacy measurement from imagery.

additionalSearches.query: global housing deficit estimate inadequate housing billion people (2024 onward)
additionalSearches.finding: 3,840 works: The Global Housing Crisis (2024), national deficit studies (Nigeria), housing affordability measurement. Deficits are documented; no solution at global scale.

additionalSearches.query: low-cost housing 3D printed homes cost evaluation (2024 onward)
additionalSearches.finding: 2,300 works including a 2026 review of 3D-printed construction scalability for affordable housing (Kuwait), financing studies and Monte Carlo planning for 3D-printed rural housing; costs and scale unproven.

additionalSearches.query: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana Gramin evaluation houses built (2024 onward)
additionalSearches.finding: 39 works: regional impact studies (Manipur, Jammu and Doda) and comparisons with Indira Awas Yojana. A large national programme exists, but evaluations are local and descriptive.

additionalSearches.query: UN-Habitat inadequate housing 2.8 billion people slums 1.1 billion (2024 onward)
additionalSearches.finding: 44 works: satellite mapping of slum expansion during COVID-19 (2026), ADB affordable housing approach 2026-2030; no global solution.
About 100 million homeless; one in four live in harmful conditions; 3 billion people (40%) will need adequate housing by 2030; 96,000 new affordable units needed every day.
